1: \section{Abstract confidence transport}\label{sec:abstract-transport}
2: 
3: The argument is easiest to read as a sequence of interfaces.  A statistical
4: model supplies confidence in a frozen, predictable metric.  Geometry transports
5: that confidence to the current relinearized metric.  An operator certificate
6: then relates the current metric to the SPD operator used for scoring, and a
7: solver certificate relates exact operator widths to the numerical widths seen
8: by the action selector.  This section states that composition abstractly;
9: \Cref{sec:corrected-center} supplies the primary squared-loss confidence model.
10: 
11: \paragraph{Protocol and timing.}
12: Let $(\mathsf A,\mathcal B)$ be a standard Borel action space.  At round $t$,
13: the learner observes a context and a nonempty random action correspondence
14: $\cA_t:\Omega\to 2^{\mathsf A}$ whose graph
15: \[
16:  \operatorname{Gr}(\cA_t)
17:  :=\{(\omega,a):a\in\cA_t(\omega)\}
18:  \in\cHist_t^-\otimes\mathcal B.
19: \]
20: Here $\cHist_t^-$ is the history after the context and action correspondence
21: are observed but before fresh round-$t$ algorithmic randomization.  The variable
22: $\Omega_t$ records all round-$t$ pre-reward randomization, which may be revealed
23: in sequential stages, and $\cHist_t=\cHist_t^-\vee\sigma(\Omega_t)$ contains
24: that randomization but not the reward.  The restrictions to
25: $\operatorname{Gr}(\cA_t)$ of
26: $(\omega,a)\mapsto\mu_t^*(a),\bq_t(a),m_t(a),b_t(a),\hat s_t(a)$, and, once
27: defined below, $U_t(a)$ are assumed jointly measurable with respect to
28: $\cHist_t\otimes\mathcal B$.  We also assume explicitly that
29: $\sup_{a\in\cA_t}\mu_t^*(a)$ and $\sup_{a\in\cA_t}U_t(a)$ are finite
30: $\cHist_t$-measurable random variables, that the oracle below returns a $\cHist_t$-measurable
31: selector in $\cA_t$, and that the simultaneous confidence and all certificate
32: events below, including path, operator, all-domain solver-upper, and
33: played-action sharpness validity, are measurable.  These are
34: substantive assumptions; standard-Borel structure
35: and graph measurability alone do not make every supremum or selector measurable.
36: 
37: Let $\bq_t(a)\in\R^d$ be the prediction query.  The three metrics are
38: \begin{align}
39:  \bVbar_1&=\lambda\bI,\nonumber\\
40:  \bVbar_{t+1}&=\bVbar_t+\sigma^{-2}\bq_t(a_t)\bq_t(a_t)^\top,
41:  \label{eq:reference-update-new}\\
42:  \bV_t&=\text{the exact current relinearized metric},\nonumber\\
43:  \Calg_t&=\text{the algorithmic SPD metric}.
44: \end{align}
45: Here $\lambda>0$ and $\sigma>0$.  Define the corresponding widths
46: \begin{equation}\label{eq:three-widths-new}
47:  \begin{aligned}
48:   \bar s_t^2(a)&=\bq_t(a)^\top\bVbar_t^{-1}\bq_t(a),\\
49:   s_t^2(a)&=\bq_t(a)^\top\bV_t^{-1}\bq_t(a),\\
50:   s_{\Calg,t}^2(a)&=\bq_t(a)^\top\Calg_t^{-1}\bq_t(a).
51:  \end{aligned}
52: \end{equation}
53: The frozen information gain is
54: \begin{equation}\label{eq:frozen-gamma-new}
55:  \gamma_T
56:  :=\log\frac{\det\bVbar_{T+1}}{\det\bVbar_1}
57:  =\sum_{t=1}^T\log\!\left(1+\sigma^{-2}\bar s_t^2(a_t)\right).
58: \end{equation}
59: Set $\gamma_0=0$, and define
60: \begin{equation}\label{eq:regret-definition-new}
61:  \operatorname{reg}_t
62:  :=\sup_{a\in\cA_t}\mu_t^*(a)-\mu_t^*(a_t),
63:  \qquad R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\operatorname{reg}_t.
64: \end{equation}
65: 
66: The reference metric $\bVbar_t$ and, when used, the representation parameter
67: $\btheta_t$ are determined from the prefix history and are
68: $\cHist_t^-$-measurable.  The exact current metric $\bV_t$ is likewise formed
69: before the fresh certificate randomization and is $\cHist_t^-$-measurable.  The realized algorithmic operator
70: $\Calg_t$, path envelope $\bar D_t$, condition factors
71: $\kappa_{-,t},\kappa_{+,t}$, solver-width map $\hat s_t(\cdot)$, sharpness
72: factor $\alpha_t$, oracle tolerance $\xi_t$, and selected action $a_t$ may
73: depend on $\Omega_t$ and are required only to be $\cHist_t$-measurable.  Thus
74: ``predictable'' below is reserved for $\cHist_t^-$-measurable quantities;
75: quantities that may use $\Omega_t$ are called pre-reward measurable.  The
76: reward is observed only after $a_t$ is selected.
77: 
78: \paragraph{How one round uses the interfaces.}
79: The prefix history determines $\bVbar_t$, $\bV_t$, and the representation used
80: to form the current queries.  Before observing the reward, the learner
81: constructs $\Calg_t$, obtains its path, operator, and solver certificates,
82: forms one upper-valid width map over the score domain, and selects an action.
83: After the reward arrives, it updates the frozen rank-one statistics.  This
84: order is why confidence can use collection-time queries even though the score
85: uses current queries.  It also prevents a selected-action solver refinement
86: from changing the theorem's score without rechecking the selection guarantee.
87: 
88: \begin{assumption}[Reference confidence and operational certificates]
89: \label{asm:abstract-transport}
90: For predictable $\beta_t\ge0$ and pre-reward measurable center $m_t(a)$ and
91: action-dependent envelope $b_t(a)\ge0$, a measurable simultaneous confidence
92: event satisfies
93: \begin{equation}\label{eq:abstract-confidence-new}
94:  |\mu_t^*(a)-m_t(a)|\le\beta_t\bar s_t(a)+b_t(a)
95:  \qquad\text{for every }a\in\cA_t.
96: \end{equation}
97: There is an absolutely continuous SPD path $\bV_t(\tau)$ from
98: $\bVbar_t$ to $\bV_t$ with a pre-reward certificate
99: \begin{equation}\label{eq:path-length-new}
100:  \begin{aligned}
101:   \mathcal D_t
102:   &:=\int_0^1\!\left\|
103:   \bV_t(\tau)^{-1/2}\dot\bV_t(\tau)\bV_t(\tau)^{-1/2}
104:   \right\|_{\rm op}d\tau\\
105:   &\le\bar D_t<\infty.
106:  \end{aligned}
107: \end{equation}
108: The algorithmic operator has a pre-reward two-sided certificate
109: \begin{equation}\label{eq:operator-sandwich-new}
110:  0<\kappa_{-,t}\le\kappa_{+,t}<\infty,\qquad
111:  \kappa_{-,t}\bV_t\preceq\Calg_t\preceq\kappa_{+,t}\bV_t.
112: \end{equation}
113: Finally, the solver returns a jointly measurable pre-reward width map
114: $\hat s_t(a)\ge0$ such that, on a measurable solver event,
115: \begin{equation}\label{eq:solver-interface-new}
116:  \begin{aligned}
117:   s_{\Calg,t}(a)&\le\hat s_t(a)
118:   &&\text{for every }a\in\cA_t,\\
119:   \hat s_t(a_t)&\le\alpha_t s_{\Calg,t}(a_t),
120:   &&\alpha_t\ge1.
121:  \end{aligned}
122: \end{equation}
123: The first condition is an all-domain optimism certificate.  The second is
124: required only at the played action.
125: \end{assumption}
126: 
127: Use the transported score
128: \begin{equation}\label{eq:transported-score-new}
129:  U_t(a)=m_t(a)
130:  +\beta_t e^{\bar D_t/2}\sqrt{\kappa_{+,t}}\,\hat s_t(a)
131:  +b_t(a),
132: \end{equation}
133: and let a pre-reward oracle return a $\cHist_t$-measurable selector
134: $a_t\in\cA_t$ satisfying
135: \begin{equation}\label{eq:approx-score-oracle-new}
136:  U_t(a_t)\ge\sup_{a\in\cA_t}U_t(a)-\xi_t,\qquad \xi_t\ge0.
137: \end{equation}
138: Regret is defined against the mean-reward supremum, so an optimal action need
139: not exist.
140: 
141: \begin{remark}[One realized solver-width map]
142: The all-domain solver upper condition, the played-action sharpness condition,
143: and the approximate-score-oracle inequality refer to the same realized width
144: map $\hat s_t(\cdot)$.  Refining the selected action's solve after selection
145: must not silently replace the value used in $U_t(a_t)$.  If refinement changes
146: $\hat s_t(a_t)$, the oracle inequality must be checked again, or the original
147: score width must remain the theorem object.  Any randomized post-selection
148: verification needs its own pre-draw filtration and conditional failure
149: allocation.  No all-action sharpness condition is required.
150: \end{remark}

174: \begin{theorem}[Estimator- and solver-agnostic confidence transport]
175: \label{thm:transported-ucb}
176: Under the protocol above with $\lambda>0$ and $\sigma>0$, suppose
177: \Cref{asm:abstract-transport} holds, the score obeys
178: \eqref{eq:transported-score-new}--\eqref{eq:approx-score-oracle-new}, and
179: $\|\bq_t(a)\|_2\le G$.  On the joint confidence and certificate event, the
180: instantaneous regret satisfies
181: \begin{equation}\label{eq:instantaneous-transport-new}
182:  \operatorname{reg}_t\le
183:  \beta_t\!\left[1+\alpha_t e^{\bar D_t}
184:  \sqrt{\frac{\kappa_{+,t}}{\kappa_{-,t}}}\right]\bar s_t(a_t)
185:  +2b_t(a_t)+\xi_t.
186: \end{equation}
187: Consequently,
188: \begin{align}
189: R_T
190: &\le
191: \sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)\gamma_T
192: \sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t^2
193: \left[1+\alpha_t e^{\bar D_t}
194: \sqrt{\frac{\kappa_{+,t}}{\kappa_{-,t}}}\right]^2}
195: \nonumber\\[-1mm]
196: &\quad+2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.\label{eq:sharp-transport-regret-new}
197: \end{align}
198: In particular, the simpler bound
199: \begin{align}
200: R_T
201: &\le2\sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)\gamma_T
202: \sum_{t=1}^T\alpha_t^2\beta_t^2e^{2\bar D_t}
203: \frac{\kappa_{+,t}}{\kappa_{-,t}}}
204: \nonumber\\[-1mm]
205: &\quad+2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t
206: \label{eq:simple-transport-regret-new}
207: \end{align}
208: holds.  The bias envelope enters twice and the approximate-oracle error enters
209: once.  If the confidence event has probability at least $1-\delta$ and the
210: joint certificate event has probability at least $1-\delta_{\rm cert}$, these
211: bounds hold with probability at least $1-\delta-\delta_{\rm cert}$.
212: \end{theorem}
213: 
214: \begin{proposition}[Frozen-width UCB on its own trajectory]
215: \label{prop:frozen-width-ucb}
216: Keep the timing, measurability, bounded-query, and frozen-update assumptions
217: above, and assume \eqref{eq:abstract-confidence-new} along the trajectory of
218: the policy that uses
219: \[
220:  U_t^{\rm fr}(a)=m_t(a)+\beta_t\bar s_t(a)+b_t(a).
221: \]
222: Assume its score supremum is finite and measurable and its pre-reward
223: measurable selector satisfies
224: $U_t^{\rm fr}(a_t)\ge\sup_{a\in\cA_t}U_t^{\rm fr}(a)-\xi_t$.
225: On the reference-confidence event,
226: \begin{align}
227:  \operatorname{reg}_t
228:  &\le 2\beta_t\bar s_t(a_t)+2b_t(a_t)+\xi_t,\nonumber\\
229:  R_T
230:  &\le 2\sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)
231:  \gamma_T\sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t^2}
232:  +2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
233:  \label{eq:frozen-width-regret}
234: \end{align}
235: All quantities are evaluated on this policy's own selected history.  No path,
236: current-metric, or operator certificate is needed for this score.  If its
237: reference-confidence event has probability at least $1-\delta$, so does this
238: guarantee.
239: \end{proposition}
240: 
241: \begin{proposition}[Reference-width floor on a fixed history]
242: \label{prop:reference-width-floor}
243: On the certificate event of \Cref{asm:abstract-transport}, every scored action
244: satisfies
245: \begin{equation}\label{eq:reference-width-floor}
246:  w_t^{\rm tr}(a):=e^{\bar D_t/2}\sqrt{\kappa_{+,t}}\hat s_t(a)
247:  \ge \bar s_t(a).
248: \end{equation}
249: For exact current widths, the actionwise multiplier
250: \begin{equation}\label{eq:actionwise-width-ratio}
251:  c_t(a)=\begin{cases}
252:  \bar s_t(a)/s_t(a),&\bq_t(a)\ne0,\\
253:  1,&\bq_t(a)=0
254:  \end{cases}
255:  \qquad\text{satisfies}\qquad c_t(a)s_t(a)=\bar s_t(a).
256: \end{equation}
257: Thus this exact actionwise correction reproduces the frozen-width score when
258: the center, radius, and bias are the same.
259: 
260: More generally, fix an action and $m_t(a)$, $b_t(a)$, $\beta_t>0$, and
261: $\bar s_t(a)$.  If the only restriction on its mean is the full interval
262: \eqref{eq:abstract-confidence-new}, a score
263: $m_t(a)+\beta_t w_t(a)+b_t(a)$ is an upper bound for every mean in that
264: interval if and only if $w_t(a)\ge\bar s_t(a)$.
265: \end{proposition}
266: 
267: The last statement concerns the uncertainty set supplied by one confidence
268: band.  Additional restrictions on the mean, a different center, or another
269: simultaneous confidence event can change that set.  An exact scalar endpoint
270: distance supplies a worst-direction multiplier, not necessarily the
271: actionwise equality in \eqref{eq:actionwise-width-ratio}.  These are
272: same-history comparisons; they do not order the realized regret of policies
273: whose actions and subsequent histories differ.
274: Evaluating the ratio in \eqref{eq:actionwise-width-ratio} as written uses the
275: reference width itself and supplies no computational shortcut.  This
276: observation is not a general computational lower bound.
277: 
278: \begin{remark}[The reference band alone does not justify a smaller width]
279: \label{rem:naive-width-band-counterexample}
280: Consider an abstract confidence-band instance with $D>0$,
281: $\bVbar=\bI_2$, $\bV=\operatorname{diag}(e^D,e^{-D})$, and
282: $\bq=(1,0)^\top$.  Take $m=b=0$, $\beta>0$, and $\mu^*=\beta$.
283: Then $\bar s=1$ and $s=e^{-D/2}$, so
284: \[
285:  |\mu^*-m|=\beta\bar s+b,\qquad
286:  m+\beta s+b=\beta e^{-D/2}<\mu^*.
287: \]
288: Reference confidence therefore holds while the naive current-width score is
289: not an upper bound.  This illustrates the limited-information statement of
290: \Cref{prop:reference-width-floor}; it does not construct a realizable
291: scaled-tanh learning trajectory or establish that this certificate family was
292: necessary in the reported runs.
293: \end{remark}
294:

296: $D=\log 4$ and $\beta=1$.  The support of a metric unit ball in direction
297: $\bq$ is the corresponding inverse-metric width.  Here that support shrinks

315: \begin{corollary}[Measurably enumerated finite domains]
316: \label{cor:finite-enumeration-new}
317: Suppose there is a positive $\cHist_t^-$-measurable integer $K_t$ and
318: $\cHist_t^-$-measurable actions $a_{t,k}:\Omega\to\mathsf A$, $k\ge1$, such
319: that
320: \[
321:  \cA_t=\{a_{t,1},\ldots,a_{t,K_t}\}.
322: \]
323: If the learner chooses the smallest index attaining the score maximum, then the
324: selected action is $\cHist_t$-measurable and
325: \eqref{eq:approx-score-oracle-new} holds with $\xi_t=0$.  The score and
326: mean-reward suprema and the universal actionwise events reduce to measurable
327: finite maxima and intersections.  A fixed finite action set is the immediate
328: special case.
329: \end{corollary}
330: 
331: The theorem separates validity from usefulness.  Reference confidence and the
332: all-domain upper width make the score optimistic.  The reverse metric and
333: operator comparisons, together with played-action sharpness, return the
334: selected width to the frozen potential and produce the closed regret bound.
335: Large $\bar D_t$, a small $\kappa_{-,t}$, loose solver sharpness, persistent
336: bias, or oracle error can still make that bound uninformative.  No optimizer
337: residual, CG-specific formula, or dynamic-width complexity appears in the
338: headline result.  The displayed closed bound requires a positive lower
339: operator factor: an upper comparison alone does not supply the return
340: comparison used in its proof.
341: 
342: \begin{algorithm}[t]
343: \caption{Corrected-center specialization of transported UCB}\label{alg:transported-ucb}
344: \begin{algorithmic}[1]
345: \STATE Observe the context and graph-measurable action correspondence $\cA_t$; this defines $\cHist_t^-$.
346: \STATE Take the prefix-determined $\btheta_t$, $\bVbar_t$, and $\bV_t$; using the observed context, form $\bq_t(a)$, $m_t^{\rm corr}(a)$, and $b_t(a)$.
347: \STATE Choose $\cHist_t^-$-measurable failure budgets before their corresponding draws; reveal the pre-reward randomness $\Omega_t$.
348: \STATE Construct $\Calg_t$ and obtain pre-reward certificates $\bar D_t$, $\kappa_{-,t}$, and $\kappa_{+,t}$.
349: \STATE Obtain one jointly measurable solver upper-width map $\hat s_t(a)$ over the score domain.
350: \STATE Return a $\cHist_t$-measurable $\xi_t$-approximate selector for the score in \eqref{eq:transported-score-new}.
351: \STATE Observe the reward; update the frozen ridge estimator and \eqref{eq:reference-update-new}.
352: \end{algorithmic}
353: \end{algorithm}
354: 
355: Algorithm~\ref{alg:transported-ucb} specifies interfaces rather than a single
356: linear algebra implementation.  Exact Cholesky solves satisfy the solver
357: interface directly in exact arithmetic.  Matrix-free CG instead holds one SPD
358: operator fixed and uses curvature--vector products to solve each action system;
359: a residual or energy argument must certify the returned widths.  Replacing the
360: operator by a window, subsample, or sketch is a separate approximation and
361: requires its own operator comparison.  The controlled experiment in
362: \Cref{sec:transport-instantiation} uses dense exact-current matrices and
363: Cholesky solves, so it does not evaluate these approximate or matrix-free paths.

365: \section{Logarithmic transport for relinearized curvature}
366: \label{sec:logarithmic-transport}
367: 
368: \begin{lemma}[Logarithmic comparison along an SPD path]
369: \label{lem:log-spd-path}
370: Let $\bV:[0,1]\to\mathbb{S}_{++}^d$ be entrywise absolutely continuous and
371: let $\dot\bV(\tau)$ denote its almost-everywhere derivative.  If
372: \begin{equation}\label{eq:generic-path-length-new}
373:  \mathcal D(\bV)=\int_0^1
374:  \|\bV(\tau)^{-1/2}\dot\bV(\tau)\bV(\tau)^{-1/2}\|_{\rm op}\,d\tau,
375: \end{equation}
376: then
377: \begin{equation}\label{eq:log-path-sandwich-new}
378:  e^{-\mathcal D(\bV)}\bV(0)\preceq\bV(1)
379:  \preceq e^{\mathcal D(\bV)}\bV(0).
380: \end{equation}
381: No commutativity or small-path assumption is required.
382: \end{lemma}
383: 
384: \begin{remark}[Thompson distance and selected-path length]
385: The integrand in \eqref{eq:generic-path-length-new} is the classical Thompson
386: Finsler norm on the positive-definite cone
387: \citep{thompson1963certain,nussbaum1994finsler}.  Its endpoint metric is
388: \[
389:  d_{\rm Th}(A,B)
390:  :=\inf\{r\ge0:e^{-r}A\preceq B\preceq e^rA\}.
391: \]
392: Equivalently,
393: \[
394:  d_{\rm Th}(A,B)
395:  =\left\|\log(A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2})\right\|_{\rm op}.
396: \]
397: Therefore \Cref{lem:log-spd-path} gives
398: \begin{align*}
399:  d_{\rm Th}(\bV(0),\bV(1))&\le\mathcal D(\bV),\\
400:  d_{\rm Th}(\bVbar_t,\bV_t)&\le\mathcal D_t\le\bar D_t.
